newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-FIFA SAYS WORLD CUP TRUCE MAKES NO DIFFERENCE TO BIDDING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA SAYS WORLD CUP TRUCE MAKES NO DIFFERENCE TO BIDDING.

text.p: World soccer body FIFA said on Friday the truce reached by UEFA and the English Football Association (F.A.) over the 2006 World Cup finals would not make any difference to the bidding process.
"Before the meeting we had a set of statutes. Now, after the meeting, those statutes still apply," FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper said.
"Every national football association has the right to bid for the 2006 World Cup finals. That right still exists. (The meeting) really re-affirmed what is and what has always been the status quo."
"It is not for a federation to change FIFA rules. They're not for anybody else to change other than the FIFA congress."
Cooper said FIFA was pleased the three-hour talks between UEFA and English officials earlier on Friday had taken some of the bitterness out of a potentially explosive issue.
"It's good that the situation has been largely cleared up and that the polemics have been taken out of it," he said.
FIFA will invite official bids for the 2006 finals in November 1998. The deadline is February 1999 and a venue for the tournament will be announced in June 2000.
Any talk of official bids before November 1998 is premature, Cooper insisted: "Until then there are simply statements of interest from the various associations."
He said England and Germany were the only two European countries so far to have expressed an interest in hosting the finals.
